title: Basic biology
description: The fundamental concepts of biology, linked to each other.

cards.back: The smallest unit of a living being. It has a membrane, cytoplasm and genetic material ([[DNA]]); it can be prokaryotic, without a nucleus, or eukaryotic, with a nucleus.
Deoxyribonucleic acid: the molecule that stores genetic information. It is a double helix of nucleotides (A, T, C, G); the stretches that code for proteins are called genes (see [[Gene]]).
A stretch of [[DNA]] containing the information to make a protein or a functional RNA. It is the unit of heredity.
Division of a [[Cell]] into two daughter cells identical to the mother cell, with the same number of chromosomes. It serves growth and tissue repair.
Cell division that produces gametes, with half the chromosomes of the mother cell. It reshuffles the genes ([[Gene]]) and creates variability.
The process by which plants, algae and some bacteria use light to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen. It takes place in an organelle, the [[Chloroplast]].
Organelle of plant cells that contains chlorophyll and carries out [[Photosynthesis]].
Organelle that produces most of the cell's energy (ATP) through [[Cellular respiration]]. It has its own DNA.
Process that, in the [[Mitochondrion]], breaks down glucose with oxygen to produce ATP, releasing carbon dioxide and water.
A protein that speeds up a chemical reaction in the body without being consumed. It acts on a specific substrate.
Mechanism of [[Evolution]] described by Darwin: individuals with traits better suited to the environment survive and reproduce more, passing those traits on.
Change in the inherited traits of populations over generations, driven above all by [[Natural selection]].
An organism's ability to keep internal conditions (temperature, blood sugar, pH) stable as external ones change.
